page: Vultr vc2-2c-4gb is a shared-resource virtual machine from the Cloud Compute product line. The hardware architecture utilizes a 64-bit x86 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, provisioning two virtual CPUs mapped to a single physical core via hyperthreading. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is fixed at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. The server does not include GPU acceleration. Storage is locally bundled with an 80 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark profiles reflect an entry-tier configuration subject to hypervisor-level CPU sharing. Synthetic processing evaluations record a single-core stress-ng result of 1226.09 and a multi-core score of 2501.8. Geekbench scores reach 738.0 for single-core and 1322.0 for multi-core, with PassMark measuring CPU throughput at 2470.92 and memory operations at 1227.87. Memory bandwidth tests yield 176.23 GB/sec on cached small blocks, decreasing to 19.26 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 16.87 GB/sec for large writes. In operational tests, static web serving achieves 1.8 GB/sec, while in-memory Redis SET operations sustain 1.36 million operations per second.

The shared CPU allocation and modest clock frequency limit sustained heavy parallel workloads, yet the inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage provides low latency for disk-bound I/O tasks. From a resource-density perspective, the balance of two threads and 4.0 GB of RAM offers efficient infrastructure utilization for basic compute requirements. The hardware profile is best matched to light web applications, staging environments, secondary database replicas, background cron processors, and low-volume testing services.
description: Vultr vc2-2c-4gb is an entry-level virtual server within the Cloud Compute lineup, configured with two shared vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The instance is paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU, and includes 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmarks position the instance in the lower percentiles across synthetic compute tests, with a Geekbench single-core score of 738.0 and a multi-core score of 1322.0, while PassMark registers a CPU score of 2470.92. Memory bandwidth reaches 19.26 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and Redis SET throughput measures 1.36 million operations per second. Lacking a dedicated GPU and utilizing shared CPU execution, it trades peak throughput for economical compute density, making it appropriate for light web serving, staging sites, and lightweight utility services.
